claims.text: At stage-2, money in DonHang.Domain is a bare int named ...Vnd: Product.PriceVnd, OrderItem.UnitPriceVnd and Payment.AmountVnd in Entities.cs; OrderItem has public setters and no check, so it accepts a negative UnitPriceVnd.
In C#, int + int compiles whatever the variable names mean, so item.UnitPriceVnd + item.Quantity compiles at stage-2.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: arithmetic operators, addition operator +

claims.text: For a record (record class), the compiler synthesizes Equals, == and != that compare the values of the record's fields (and its EqualityContract) rather than the reference; a record declared without 'struct' is a reference type.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Records — Value equality; record class vs record struct

claims.text: At stage-3, Vnd is 'public sealed record Vnd' with a get-only Amount set only in its constructor, which throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException when amount < 0 (Vnd.cs lines 8-16).
A get-only auto-property (no set accessor) can be assigned only in a constructor or a property initializer of its type.
claims.source_hint: C# programming guide: auto-implemented properties / read-only (get-only) auto-properties

claims.text: Vnd.Plus and Vnd.Times return new(checked(...)), so each result passes through the constructor's check and neither operand changes; VndTests.Plus_ReturnsANewVnd_AndChangesNeither asserts price and fee keep their amounts.
claims.source_hint: git show stage-3:DonHang.Domain/Vnd.cs lines 21-23; DonHang.Tests/Domain/VndTests.cs lines 27-38

claims.text: In a checked context, int addition or multiplication that overflows throws OverflowException instead of wrapping around.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: checked and unchecked statements; arithmetic overflow

claims.text: Vnd defines no + operator (a record synthesizes only == and !=), so item.UnitPrice + item.Quantity with UnitPrice a Vnd and Quantity an int does not compile.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Records — synthesized members; operator overloading

claims.text: VndTests.TwoVndWithTheSameAmount_AreEqual builds two Vnd(450_000) separately and asserts Assert.Equal(a, b), a == b and !ReferenceEquals(a, b).

At stage-3, OrderItem.UnitPrice is a Vnd (comment: was int UnitPriceVnd until stage-2), and Order.Total sums items starting from Vnd.Zero with Plus and Times; CustomerId and ProductId stay int, Customer.City a string.
Wrap an int or string in its own type when a rule or a unit belongs to the value; wrapping one that carries no rule adds a type without adding a check (sections 5 and 9).
Opposing view: some teams wrap ids in their own types when two kinds of id keep getting swapped in method calls — a choice about catching mix-ups, not about a rule on the id.
Assigning a struct copies its value; a struct with a public setter still lets code change that field on its copy, so being a struct does not make a type unchanging.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: Structure types — value semantics, readonly structs

claims.text: A private set accessor can still be called from any method of the same type, so a method of Vnd could change Amount if Amount had a private setter.
claims.source_hint: C# programming guide: restricting accessor accessibility

claims.text: public static Vnd Zero { get; } = new(0); creates one instance when the type is initialized and returns that same instance on every read.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: auto-property initializers; static fields/properties initialization

claims.text: For a class with no equality of its own, == compares references, and xUnit's Assert.Equal falls back to object.Equals, so two separate instances with the same data are not equal.
claims.source_hint: xUnit assertions: Assert.Equal default comparer; C# equality comparisons (reference equality)
